data.productDescription: In-situ, sensor-based measurements of specific conductance, dissolved oxygen, pH, turbidity, fluorescent dissolved organic matter (fDOM) and chlorophyll-a, available as 1-min measurements in wadeable stream sites and 5-min measurements in lake and river sites.
data.productAbstract:
Water quality consists of a suite of physical and chemical parameters characterizing the health of an aquatic ecosystem. This data product contains in-situ, sensor-based measurements of specific conductance, dissolved oxygen, pH, turbidity, fluorescent dissolved organic matter (fDOM) and chlorophyll-a, available as 1-min measurements in wadeable stream sites and 5-min measurements in lake and river sites.  Chlorophyll-a is only measured in lake and river sites.

Latency: Data collected in any given month are published during the second full week of the following month.
data.productDesignDescription:
At wadeable stream sites, multisondes are deployed at an upstream and downstream location, except for Blue River (BLUE), which only has a downstream location.  Multisondes are collocated with PRT temperature sensors at both locations, and SUNA nitrate sensor at the downstream locations.  Specific conductance, dissolved oxygen, pH and turbidity are measured at both the upstream and downstream locations, while fDOM is only measured at the downstream location.  Depth and chlorophyll-a are not measured in wadeable stream sites.  Sampling frequency for wadeable stream sites is 1-min.  At lake and river sites, the multisonde is deployed from a buoy and measures depth, specific conductance, dissolved oxygen, pH, turbidity, fDOM and chlorophyll-a.  Sampling frequency is 5-min.  At deeper lake sites (BARC, CRAM, LIRO, PRLA & TOOK) vertical profiles of the water column are collected every 4-hrs.  At the remaining lake and river sites the multisonde remains at a fixed depth of 0.5m below the water surface. 

Instrumentation:
YSI EXO2 Multiparameter Sonde with conductivity and temperature (599827), dissolved oxygen (599100), pH(599706), turbidity (599101), fDOM (599104) and chlorophyll-PC (599102) probes.
data.productStudyDescription: These data are collected at all NEON aquatic sites.
data.productBasicDescription: The basic package includes the data product, summary statistics, expanded uncertainty, and final quality flag.
data.productExpandedDescription: The expanded package includes the basic package information plus quality metrics for all of the quality assessment and quality control analyses.

changeLogs.locationAffected: All sites with buoys, meaning a HOR.VER of 103.100
changeLogs.issue: Profiling sondes from buoys do not report accurate sensorDepth values. Sonde pressure transducers are non-vented, therefore barometric pressure fluctuations also affect the sensorDepth readings, possibly at magnitudes of tens of centimeters. NEON plans to add a barometric correction to sonde sensor depth at buoy sites in a future algorithm feature.
changeLogs.resolution: Users should keep in mind that sensor depth data do not yet reflect a barometric pressure variation, so sensor depth values include additional uncertainty.

The following lists sites and corresponding dates when the sonde wiper was suspected to not be operating.
changeLogs.resolution: Firmware updates resolved the  non-wiping wiper problem.

changeLogs.issue: Sensor became exposed during low water depth
Sensor became exposed during low water depth

Safety measures to protect personnel during the COVID-19 pandemic resulted in reduced or canceled maintenance activities for extended periods at NEON sites. Data availability and/or quality may be negatively impacted during this time.

In addition, the annual refresh of sensors and data acquisition systems (DAS) did not occur according to the typical 1-year schedule for many sites. The annual refresh is where freshly calibrated and verified sensors and DAS replace the units in the field.
changeLogs.resolution:
NEON reviewed data from all sites and time periods potentially impacted by COVID-19 safety precautions to identify and manually flag suspect data that escaped automated quality tests. Suspect data are indicated by the final quality flag in the data files, which should be used to inform data filtering prior to use. 

Data during this time period should be treated as valid unless marked suspect by other quality flags. Data that are overdue for field calibrations are indicated by the validCalQF quality flag.

changeLogs.issue: Severe flooding destroyed several roads into Yellowstone National Park in June 2022, making the YELL and BLDE sites inaccessible to NEON staff. Preventive and corrective maintenance were not able to be performed, nor was the annual exchange of sensors for calibration and validation. While automated quality control routines are likely to detect and flag most issues, users are advised to review data carefully.
changeLogs.resolution: Normal operations resumed on October 31, 2022, when the National Park Service opened a newly constructed road from Gardiner, MT to Mammoth, WY with minimal restrictions. For more details about data impacts, see Data Notification https://www.neonscience.org/impact/observatory-blog/data-impacts-neons-yellowstone-sites-yell-blde-due-catastrophic-flooding-0
